## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence of the 63 documents that bears on these four policies and their base refs was traced to a source rule sentence, a parameter, an event meaning, a measure, an eligibility `applies_to`, or a tool docstring. Derived restatements (tables, boundary cases, hypothetical worked figures) entail nothing beyond their source sentences.
- Searched for added confirmations, reviews, notifications, waits or fallbacks ("confirm", "review", "notify", "please", "call", "first", "if not"): the only hits are source sentences (cancellation "which the patient confirms themselves"; "until the outside records are confirmed again"; "until the pharmacist confirms the product") and tool-contract invocation text.
- Cross-problem operational guidance: none ("if unmet, first call …" absent; no document names another problem's tool).
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none. All examples are labelled hypothetical and none reproduces task 0's rows (e.g. the clock illustrations use day 20/30/90 histories, not the task's 0/28/103).
- Additions / omissions / rewrites found: none for the policies of this task.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every atom of the four extended policies (baseline, rule sentences, every tier of every factor, params, the three prerequisites) and of their base refs (clauses in force and the retired surface) has an equivalent home; no normative KB claim lacks a source; no undeclared retirement. First revision; no prior revision exists.

Policy-side notes (reported, not a KB verdict):

- **P-1 (base clause vs extended practice).** `vax_evt_invalid_dose` keeps in force "a dose given too early elsewhere and recorded as an outside dose is simply not counted" (doc_vax_invalid_dose_standard_788cd141 standard 4), while the invalidation, opening and booking policies require an invalidation entry against every too-early dose including outside ones (task 0's E5). The visible surface resolves it (both prerequisite sentences say "every dose … given sooner than its minimum interval less the grace period"; doc_vax_early_dose_entries_taken_off_85741f79 has an explicit outside tier), so the solution stays unique; the tension originates in the source.
- **P-2 (overwrite scope).** The resumed-course policy's overwrite retires the base risk-condition clause for every course opening, while its replacement covers resumed courses only; the product chart still describes the column by its parameter_schema meaning ("Below this age the patient attests a qualifying risk condition", doc_vax_eligibility_age_thresholds_1f586e09). First-course openings below a risk age thus rest only on the schema meaning. Untriggered here (Hep B risk age 0).
- **P-3 (compute vs rule text).** The booking compute returns the earliest days ahead when the earliest date lies beyond the booking window, whereas the rule and the KB say no appointment is booked today. Untriggered (2 ≤ 30).
- **P-4 ("series history").** The source never defines "series history" when a resumed course is open; the KB mirrors that. It is resolvable (the new course holds no dose entry, so no clock can run on it; the resumed-series allowance speaks of "the course the series history is on was closed"), and GT computes on the earlier course.

Whole-corpus scan:

- Prerequisite sentences: each of the three task-0 edges' sentences stands verbatim only in its blocked hub (mechanical check over all 63 docs). Same-form restatements sit in the same document and restate states, never the resolving action, performer or problem.
- No restatement of a state-form sentence as an action; no other problem's tool named in any hub (each of the six task tool names occurs only in its own hub); no route, checklist, roadmap or ordered multi-problem step list; no aggregated dependency table. The booking hub's "Standing conditions" groups only that policy's own two source sentences.
- Depended-on documents are reachable through record and sentence words ("invalidation entry", "restated", "stands open … with its opening doses still needed", "signed screening and consent form"), not only through dependent-document phrasing; their use of the sentence's words is what the forward scan requires.
- Titles and openings name general subjects (e.g. "Immunization Services - Opening a Resumed Vaccination Course", "Immunization Services Action Card - Dose Invalidation Entries"); none mirrors task 0's situation (out-of-state clinic dose, earliest-date booking).
- Factor documents: none states which tier customers fall on, names a mistake to avoid, or writes task evidence rows in as fact.
- Computation documents and factor documents that name other quantities, examined and not RED because the named text is the source's own: doc_vax_opening_doses_still_needed_8a05dc61 cl. 2 (the rule's result sentence "Where earlier doses are credited …"); doc_vax_next_dose_appointment_date_9e28b49c ("plus Kestrel's scheduling allowance", and the rule's assembly sentence for the combined allowance); doc_vax_consent_form_dose_number_71a6af11 §2 (the rule's positions definition, a base-computation intermediate bound to no factor); doc_vax_carrying_earlier_doses_1872e21e (the declared overwrite's replaced_by sentence naming the credit window and credit rules); doc_vax_restatement_bases_119ca3e7, doc_vax_scheduling_allowance_combination_6dd5ea77, doc_vax_dose_numbering_on_continued_series_b26c54c3 (their own ladder texts). Policy-side note: because the source's assembly and ladder sentences name the factor quantities, the computation documents necessarily tell a reader that credits, allowances and position counts exist. Each fall-back is still definite (3 / 3 / 1 / 1).

**Verdict: PASS.**
